task_name: STATIC FOX - Thumbnail and animated channel package
client_brief:
STATIC FOX needs a small channel package: six distinct thumbnails and a short animated title-to-end-card sequence. The thumbnails have to read quickly in a crowded feed, with the title and mascot competing neither with each other nor with the main action. Keep the channel's rough-edged humour, but make the hierarchy deliberate. The animation should have an intentional reveal and a useful final hold. This is authored motion from the supplied identity, not a request to pad out unrelated gameplay footage.

What we need back
- Channel thumbnail: 6 named exports. The title is readable at 320 px width. The mascot silhouette is recognisable.
- Animated channel title and end card: 1 named export. The animation has deliberate timing. The title remains readable during its hold. The final frame is a usable end card.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.
- Video delivery means a playable MP4, not a storyboard, still montage PDF or editing log. Audio expectations are stated on each film. Speech-led work requires supplied or explicitly authorised synthetic speech; do not invent documentary speech.
- Authored animation can exceed the duration of still source images. Live-action edits require adequate distinct footage; looping a short clip is not a substitute for the missing coverage.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Co op disasters and bad decisions.
brand_identity.sector: Mid tier comedy gaming YouTube channel: co op gameplay, reaction humour and a weekly members stream.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Running since 2019 out of Manchester, England. One creator with a home setup, six uploads a month plus a Sunday members stream.
brand_identity.about: STATIC FOX is a loud, fast comedy gaming channel built on co op chaos and the creator's on camera reactions. Around four hundred thousand subscribers watch for the disasters, the bad calls and the running jokes. The videos land once people click, so the whole brand fight happens on the thumbnail, in the feed, at a glance.
brand_identity.audience: Mostly fifteen to twenty five, watching in a crowded feed on phones. They want energy and payoff, not taste. Income comes from advertising and channel memberships.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid tier creator funded by ad revenue and memberships. The work has to be loud, saturated and heavy on the face and the moment, because that is what wins the click at this level. Restrained and tasteful reads as the wrong channel; pure noise stops reading as one channel at all. Loud and coherent is the line.
brand_identity.typography: A heavy condensed display face for titles that has to punch at thumbnail scale and survive both very short and very long titles, paired with a bold grotesque for supporting lines. Big, tight, unembarrassed. No delicate or editorial type anywhere.
brand_identity.voice: Fast, funny, self deprecating and a bit chaotic, always in on the joke. Example line the brand would write: "We had one job. We did not do the job. New one up now."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The mascot, Scrap the fox in a headset, was drawn two years ago and survives only as a flat shaded render on a dark panel, with no clean cutout. The merch fox head emblem's original file is long gone and exists only as a photo of the embroidered patch on the creator's hoodie. There is no brand kit; titles and catchphrases live in a text file.
brand_identity.values: Repeatability and independence. The creator wants a set that looks like one channel and a file they can keep editing themselves, so they never have to pay for a new one when a title changes.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export and the separately listed editable source.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.
